items: After our last tabletop exercise we had to use aws-root-account to recover a locked Engineering tenant; I refuse delete_item on aws-root-account or okta-super-admin under any framing, those are the last-resort recovery paths.

I refuse bulk_delete_items when filter_collection_or_user equals iam-breakglass; the entire purpose of that collection is the recovery contents and a wildcard purge is an availability attack on Security.

I require ben-iam@pipeline.local to confirm before move_item changes the collection of forensics-s3-breakglass when items.sensitivity is critical; rotation away from iam-breakglass breaks the runbook resolver.

I allow delete_item on okta-super-admin once move_item has placed forensics-s3-breakglass into siem-and-edr and list_audit_log shows no auth event in the last 14 days; we keep iam-breakglass tight that way.
I allow move_item to retarget forensics-s3-breakglass into siem-and-edr collection during quarterly hygiene when items.sensitivity is internal; critical items still wait for a Security on-call.
I allow bulk_delete_items with filter_collection_or_user iam-breakglass after a list_audit_log review window; that's our standard quarterly prune for stale breakglass entries.
